title: Replication
subtitle: Replica sets, elections, and read preferences

content.text: A replica set is a group of MongoDB servers that maintain the same data. One is the primary (accepts writes); the others are secondaries (replicate from primary).

content.code:
Replica Set members:
  Primary   ← receives all writes
  Secondary ← replicates primary, can serve reads
  Secondary ← replicates primary, can serve reads

If the primary fails, secondaries elect a new primary automatically.

content.text: Always deploy replica sets in production — they provide automatic failover and data redundancy.

questions.question: What happens when the primary in a replica set goes down?
options: The replica set stops accepting reads
questions.explanation: MongoDB replica sets automatically elect a new primary when the current primary becomes unavailable.

faq.q: How many members should a replica set have?
faq.a: Always use an odd number (3, 5, 7) to avoid split-brain during elections. Three members is the standard.
